newsitem.title: UK: BOE against joint regulator for banks, securities.
newsitem.headline: BOE against joint regulator for banks, securities.

text.p: Bank of England deputy governor Howard Davies said the central bank remained unpersuaded by arguments that there should be a single regulatory body for both banks and securities houses.
In a speech prepared for delivery in Liverpool, he discussed suggestions that the business of banks and securities firms had become sufficiently intertwined to justify a single regulator.
"I must say that we are not persuaded," Davies said.

"In our view there is still a reasonably clear distinction to be made between banks and other financial institutions, and their prudential soundness, or lack of it, can have rather different implications for the rest of the market."
There was a clear difference between the asset and liability structure of commercial banks and securities firms, while banks, unlike securities firms, were at the heart of the payments system.
"Their failure can therefore have a very direct and profound impact on the wider economy," he added.

The BoE aimed to ensure that the costs of regulation were minimised and that cooperation between regulators was "based on a clear understanding of responsibilities and the free flow of information," Davies added.
